source.title: Probing Unlearned Diffusion Models: A Transferable Adversarial Attack Perspective
source.authors: Xiaoxuan Han; Songlin Yang; Wei Wang; Yang Li; Jing Dong

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix are present. The extraction has page-break and figure artifacts, and some comparison tables are flattened; no substantive cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests concept-erasure robustness and restoration attacks on text-to-image diffusion models, a different model setting from the LLM claim.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates adversarial embedding restoration and prompt-level restoration attacks on unlearned diffusion models. It does not test LLM unlearning, fine-tuning on unrelated or loosely related examples, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or newer counter-methods. Table values for the paper's own attack are recorded below; several flattened baseline-comparison values are omitted where the method-to-value alignment is not secure.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether concept-erased Stable Diffusion v1.4 models (UCE, ESD, FMN, CA) still produce erased concepts under embedding-level and prompt-level attacks. This is a new setting: text-to-image diffusion rather than LLMs. Its results bear on A, on C's 'blocks access rather than deletes' clause, and on E through the prompt-level baselines. The main attack is optimization-based (adversarial textual-inversion search on the original SD, transferred black-box), not a 'simple' attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also state that erasure methods only shift the text-to-image mapping and keep the visual content in the generative space. They say prompt-level attacks struggle on narrow concepts, while their black-box transferable embedding restores objects, styles, nudity and identities across UCE, ESD, FMN and CA.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses concept-erasure methods and adversarial embedding search on Stable Diffusion; it does not reproduce LLM unlearning recipes. Its proposed attack alternates embedding search and model updates on the original Stable Diffusion surrogate.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with target concept and erasure method. The study also reports that restoration embeddings found without Adversarial Search struggle for most erasure methods, while the with-search score increases over optimization epochs; the CA-erased case is an exception described in Section 4.3 and Figure 10.
record.problems: The evidence concerns text-to-image diffusion models, not LLMs. Results are classifier-based and chance levels are not stated. No general-ability retention test is reported. Several baseline-comparison table values are flattened in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The flattened comparison results for baseline restoration methods in Tables 1 and 3 are not individually extracted where method-to-value alignment is uncertain. Qualitative prompt-level outcomes are retained in R53-R57. Figure 10's epoch-by-epoch values are figure-only; the text describes their direction but supplies no numeric scores.

untested.parts: Retention of general ability or image quality on non-target prompts is not measured. LLM knowledge unlearning is not tested.
Entirely untested; there is no fine-tuning or relearning of the unlearned model.
No activation-direction ablation and no weight or activation analysis of the unlearned models. The 'blocks access' evidence is input-embedding recovery plus authors' assertion.
Entirely untested; there is no quantization.
No rephrasing, other languages or in-context information. Only optimized adversarial prompts (UnlearnDiff, Ring-A-Bell) are tested.
Entirely untested; no robust counter-method is proposed or evaluated.

missing.what: Embedding attack on Car (98/99/91/100 versus w/o 16/21/72/80) and Jeep (99/99/97/99 versus 4/4/39/0)
Numeric prompt-level attack values; RAB and UD columns are recoverable and alignment is resolvable
White-box Concept Inversion embedding attacks recovering concepts, e.g. CI(ESD) Jeep 81-98
Original SD reference levels with and without attack (e.g. Picasso 30.0, Monet 100.0)
Ablation: embeddings without Adversarial Search fail on most erasure methods except CA

record.verdict_notes: The setting is diffusion models, not LLMs, so all links are a cross-modality T3 extension. The reader's version codes (V1/V3/V5) were invalid and have been remapped. The main attack is a learned continuous embedding optimized on the original SD, not a simple attack; it sits between C and E. It is linked to A and C as the reader did, but could arguably be filed as a soft-prompt attack under E. No general-ability check and no uncertainty are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure retention of general ability. The study tests diffusion concept erasure and whether restoration attacks recover the target, not LLM unlearning.
No fine-tuning or relearning of the unlearned model using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation. The study argues that concept erasure shifts the text-to-image mapping while preserving visual content, and tests embedding-level restoration.
Tests prompt-level adversarial restoration methods, not simple rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
No newer counter-method intended to resist the listed attacks.

relationships.condition: Transferred adversarial embedding attack (black-box, from original SD) on UCE/ESD/FMN/CA-erased SD v1.4
relationships.reason: Erased concepts return at high classifier rates, e.g. Dog 96-100, Brad Pitt 81.5-97, Jolie 70.5-99 (R01, R02, R04, R14, R16, R19, R20, R28, R31, R32, R34-R45, R48, R51, R52). Note that the attack is optimization-based, not simple.
relationships.display_finding: Optimization-based embedding attacks restored erased concepts, with classifier rates of 81.5–97 for Brad Pitt and 70.5–99 for Jolie.

labels.reason: Authors say erasure shifts the mapping and keeps the content. The evidence is indirect, with no internal-edit analysis.

FMN barely erases Dog, English Springer and nudity (65/69/56 with no attack).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Proposed adversarial embedding restoration across the tested concepts and erasure methods
reader_labels.reason: The proposed attack raises target-concept classifier scores above the no-attack baseline in the reported settings; see R01-R52, though some gains are partial and some baseline scores were already high.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Pre-attack outcomes for some concept-erasure settings
reader_labels.reason: Some tested models already show substantial target accuracy without an attack, so not every erasure setting begins near chance; see R03, R07, and R15.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Embedding-level adversarial restoration on the tested diffusion concepts
reader_labels.reason: The study reports restoration after embedding-level attacks and argues that erasure shifts mappings while leaving visual content in the model's generative space; see R01-R52.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper says prompt-level attacks are effective for broad-object restoration; see R53.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Prompt-level attacks on narrow objects, artist styles, and celebrity identities
reader_labels.reason: The paper describes prompt-level restoration as ineffective for these concept groups; see R54, R55, and R57.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Prompt-level restoration works for some erasure methods but fails for others, including UCE; see R56.
